title: Both defects in the brief were already fixed. The city still froze itself — it was out of coal, not off the grid

the_brief_was_stale_and_i_proved_it_by_r.defect 1 — 'opens 93% black, 19/255': ALREADY FIXED at HEAD by 7591703 (last wave). Re-measured, same scenario, same shot: opening.world.png 32.61/255, opening.png 52.48/255. ClimateProfile.opening_tick = 2016 puts a new game in mid-morning; the HUD reads 'Morning -18C Overcast, NIGHTFALL IN 3:25'. I changed nothing here.
the_brief_was_stale_and_i_proved_it_by_r.defect 2 — 'watchtower (142,119) and tur: ALREADY FIXED at HEAD by c690b03 (last wave). Re-ran the E5 probe verbatim: ONE heat network, both defences on it, power_factor 1.00 and no 'unreachable' from t=20, nothing frozen at t=600 or t=2000. The cells in the brief (142,119)/(142,137) do not even exist any more; the `fed` helper now derives them to (140,118)/(141,138).
the_brief_was_stale_and_i_proved_it_by_r.the check the brief asked for also exist: boot.opening_defects() — every heat consumer on a network with no source of heat, read off the BUILT WORLD, Log.error on every launch, asserted by tests/f3.
the_brief_was_stale_and_i_proved_it_by_r.so i did not redo it: I re-verified rather than re-implemented, and then went looking for why the critic's sentence was still true.

what_was_actually_still_broken.the sentence: 'the opening settlement fails on its own before the player touches it. That is not pressure, that is a broken save.' Still true at HEAD. Twenty minutes later on the clock, and worse.
what_was_actually_still_broken.measured, seed 7, boot's own layout, una: coal stock 200 -> 0 by t≈1800. The Hearth's bunker emptied at t≈4700. watchtower froze t=5310, turret_mount t=5364 — THE SAME TWO BUILDINGS, one wave later, for a different reason. warmth_radiator x2 t=6068/6084, housing_block x2 t=6224, THE HEARTH ITSELF t=6317, coal_generator t=6318, workshop t=6794. Eight buildings, and it never recovered: supply 0.0 and twelve frozen at t=12000, avg_warmth 15-24.
what_was_actually_still_broken.the Hearth's own description: 'It burns anything and it never stops. If it goes out, the city does.' It went out on every single new game, at minute five, with 320 scrap sitting in the yard.
what_was_actually_still_broken.the cause: the opening layout shipped 200 coal and NO income of coal, timber or scrap. No extractor of any kind. The city was a battery with no charger.
what_was_actually_still_broken.the thing that makes the obvious fix not: I tried the salvage loop first — 2 scrap_collectors + 2 rubble_sorters, fed off the trunk. It RUNS (scrap 320->270, timber regenerating 106->126 between t=2400 and t=3600) and the city still froze at t=5400, because HeatDef._first_fuel keeps only fuel_items[0] and HeatSystem.deliver_fuel rejects everything else. The Hearth's declared `fuel_items = [coal, timber]` is dead data: it eats coal and nothing else. See the open items — that is [P02]'s.

what_i_changed.game/boot.gd — the coal road: the opening now ships the loop it runs on: an ore_drill on the coal seam and the pipe road home. Neither is typed. `coal_seam()` asks [P01] where the coal is (MapGenerator pins the first cluster of every kind to the inner band on purpose — its own comment is 'on a real run means the player's first coal is ninety tiles from the hearth'). `road_to_core()` WALKS the core flow field back from the seam — the same field a citizen walks — expanding every diagonal into two orthogonal steps, because heat does not conduct across a corner.
what_i_changed.why the road is walked and not drawn: my FIRST version was a typed L of two straight runs. It drove the pipe into a ridge on 2 of 8 seeds, broke in the middle, and left the drill alone on network 2 — the watchtower's bug again, one wave later, inside the code written to prevent it. opening_defects() caught it, which is the entire argument for having a gate. Grid.TERRAIN_FLAGS sets F_WALK and F_BUILD on exactly the same six terrains, so a walkable path is a buildable one; tests/f3 asserts that pairing instead of assuming it.
what_i_changed.game/boot.gd — the layout now tracks its: the road is the one run that can arrive where the layout has already built. A pipe tile REFUSED for being occupied is a hole in a pipe, so `place`/`line` claim their footprints (sizes from the registry, not typed) and the road skips a claimed tile rather than being refused it. Refusals across 8 seeds: 10, 9, 4, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0 -> zero on all eight.
what_i_changed.game/boot.gd — opening_defects() gains i: `_unfuelled_burners`. A burner nothing in the settlement can dig or craft the fuel for is now a defect with the same teeth as a consumer off the grid: 'The Hearth at 126,126 burns coal to make 120 heat, and nothing in the opening settlement digs or crafts coal — the city runs on its starting pile and then goes out.' Connectivity and solvency are different questions and the second one is the one that ends a run.
what_i_changed.nothing in game/sim/climate/ or game/con: I read both looking for the defect and it was in neither. turret_mount's missing heat_insulation is the DEFAULT 0.35, so its self-lift is 14.6 C against the 12 C the existing test requires — not a defect. Said here because 'I checked and left it alone' is worth more than silence.

verified_by_running.the Hearth's fuel bunker: 0.0 from t≈4700 onward -> never below 22.7, holding 23-24 at t=9600/12000.
verified_by_running.eight seeds, opening placed and graded (: seeds 1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 23, 99, 1234 — every one: 1 drill placed, 1 heat network, 0 refusals, opening_defects() empty. Three of those maps the layout was never written against.
verified_by_running.tests/f3/test_opening_settlement.gd: 12 tests, 42 assertions, TESTS PASSED (was 7 tests, 27 assertions).
verified_by_running.THE REVERT CHECK: with the previous game/boot.gd restored in place, 2 of the 12 go RED and name the thing: 'the Hearth is still burning at t=9600 — it froze at t=6317 of every run before the coal road' (actual: frozen), 'nothing in the opening settlement is frozen anywhere in the first day and a half (worst: 8 at t=6600 — the_hearth at (126,126), warmth_radiator at (141,127), warmth_radiator at (114,127), housing_block at (133,131), housing_block at (119,131), coal_generator at (125,139), watchtower at (140,118), turret_mount at (141,138))', and 'the Hearth still has fuel in its bunker at t=9600' (actual 0).
verified_by_running.the gate's own red check lives IN the su: test_the_gate_names_a_hearth_with_no_coal_behind_it rebuilds the settlement with the drill taken back out — the layout that shipped last wave — and asserts the gate names the Hearth and the coal. A gate that cannot fail is not a gate.
verified_by_running.tests/boot/run_reachability.tscn --force: TESTS PASSED — 92 checks, 0 failures. 'opening settlement seeded around (128, 128)', no 'broken on arrival'.
verified_by_running.tools/determinism.sh: DETERMINISM OK — IDENTICAL on both scenarios, sha256 e2ce260c5d3d5c7a and 21edbb54e5772ddc.
verified_by_running.tools/run_sim.sh --scenario=first_night: exit 0, errors []. (The scenario builds its own city and does not use boot's layout, so this proves no collateral damage, not the fix.)
verified_by_running.tools/lint_sim.sh: 0 fatal, 1 advisory — pre-existing, [P01]'s grid_system.gd wall clock.
verified_by_running.the opening frame, photographed: artifacts/f3_boot_shot/new_game.png — the settlement BOOT really seeds, not the harness scenario, at 90 frames. HEAT GRID 77/77, +47 spare, '1 grid'. Clock: 'DAY 1 THE LULL, NIGHTFALL IN 3:25, Morning -18C Overcast'.

open: [P02], AND IT IS THE REASON THE ELEGANT FIX DID NOT WORK: a burner eats exactly one item. HeatDef._first_fuel keeps fuel_items[0] and HeatSystem.deliver_fuel(id, item, amount) returns 0 for anything else, so the_hearth.tres's `fuel_items = [coal, timber]` promises something the build does not do. Measured: with a salvage strip shipped in the opening, timber stock REGENERATED (106 -> 126 between t=2400 and t=3600) while the Hearth's bunker sat at 0.0 and the city froze at t=5400. Make deliver_fuel accept any item in fuel_items (weighted by LogiItem.fuel_value — coal 4.0, timber 2.0) and the salvage line becomes a real second answer to the fuel problem, which is the automation lesson this game is supposed to be about. I did not touch game/sim/heat/.

[P21], AND IT IS URGENT: tests/tutorial/run_tutorial.tscn is RED — 76 checks, 4 failures — and it is red because the tutorial is built on top of the defect I was sent to fix. _suite_it_opens_on_the_cold asserts `networks >= 2.0` ('the opening settlement really does stand on more than one heat network'), and _suite_time_alone_does_not_advance_it asserts `frozen >= 1` after 1200 ticks ('the structures off the mains froze by themselves — the cold is the teacher'). Lesson 01_the_pipes_reach_or_nothing_does is only OPEN while a consumer is off the grid. All four failures PRE-DATE me: networks has been 1 since last wave's c690b03, and my measurement of the pre-change layout has frozen=0 at t=600/1200/2400/3600/4320 (the first freeze was t=5310, long after the 1200-tick proof). Lesson 01 needs new material. The opening still teaches plenty — the guide's own second card is right: 'Nothing in this city makes food.'

WHY NOBODY SAW THAT FOR A WAVE, and it is a trap for everyone: `--part=tutorial` and `--part=build` and `--part=climate` all print TESTS PASSED while running ZERO tests, because those suites are standalone .tscn entry points that the in-process runner lists but does not execute ('suites 0 run, 0 skipped, 0 broken, 1 standalone / tests 0 passed'). The previous F3 reported 'tests --part=tutorial: TESTS PASSED' in good faith. Nineteen suites are standalone (`--list-standalone`). Anybody reporting a part green off `--part=` is reporting nothing for those nineteen; run the .tscn.

[P00]/tooling — THE REFERENCE SCREENSHOT SET PHOTOGRAPHS THE WRONG PHASES, and every art, VFX and UI score is graded from it. opening_tick=2016 shifts every sim tick 2016 later on the climate clock, and tests/scenarios/first_night.json's shot ticks were written for opening_tick=0. Measured with tmp/f3/phases.tscn: 'midday' lands in DUSK, 'dusk' lands in NIGHT, 'assault' lands in DEEP NIGHT, 'deep_night' lands in day 2 MORNING (broad daylight, luminance 34.7), 'dawn' lands in day 2 MORNING, 'second_night' lands in day 3 DAWN. Only 'opening' and the two 'afternoon' shots are honest. I verified corrected ticks by running them (tmp/f3/phases2.tscn): opening 30 (morning), build 900 (morning), midday 2200 (afternoon 0.50), dusk 3800 (dusk 0.46), assault 5200 (night 0.46), deep_night 6900 (deep_night 0.49), dawn 8060 (day 2 dawn 0.50), second_day_factory 11800 (afternoon 0.50), second_dusk 13400 (dusk 0.46), second_night 14800 (night 0.46), third_day_city 21400 (day 3 afternoon 0.50). The DURABLE fix is for tools/gen_scenarios.py to express a shot as a PHASE and let ClimateSystem resolve the tick, so this can never drift again. tests/scenarios/ and tools/ are not mine.

[P13], unchanged from last wave and still true: PHASE_ARC maps the START of the dawn phase onto palette 0.235, which sits 59% of the way from the night keyframe (0.19) to the dawn keyframe (0.27). The first ~336 ticks (16.8 s) of every 'Dawn' are graded mostly as night — on day 2 and every day after. opening_tick only moved where day 1 BEGINS; it cannot fix the other dawns, and the fix is one number in game/view/render/world_model.gd (dawn arc start 0.235 -> 0.27) or a palette keyframe at 0.235. That is the 'or add the keyframe' half of my brief and it is in a folder I may not write. If it lands, opening_tick can come back down toward 0 and the whole project's tick-to-phase arithmetic (see the item above) realigns for free.

[P17]: on the opening frame the ATTENTION stack shows '1 burner running dry — the city is out of coal' TWICE, once as a severity line and once as a plain one — see artifacts/f3_boot_shot/new_game.png. It is also a startup transient (nothing has fuel in its bunker at t=0 and porters take a few seconds); by t=100 both burners are loaded and the stores still read 60 coal, so 'the city is out of coal' is wrong at the moment it is shown. The stack is the best element in the project and this is the first thing a new player reads.

HONEST PRESSURE THAT REMAINS, and I left it deliberately: one drill covers the Hearth but not both burners at full tilt. From t≈9000 (day 2) the coal_generator runs dry intermittently — 'burners short of coal' in the log — and coal stock sits at 0 while the Hearth holds ~23. Nothing freezes, warmth stays 58-79. That is the player's job and it is what a second drill or a belt is FOR. I did not add a second drill; a comfortable opening would have been a different bug.

STILL DEAD IN THE OPENING: 320 scrap sits in the yard for the whole run with nothing that can process it (no rubble_sorter, no scrap_collector), the workshop stalls on `missing_input: iron_plate` forever, and research parks at 'no iron plate to be had'. That is the automation pillar (scored 2/10) with no worked example on the first screen. I deliberately did NOT ship the salvage strip in this change, because until [P02]'s multi-fuel item above is fixed it produces timber nothing can burn — it would have looked like automation and fed nothing. Once deliver_fuel takes timber, `fed.call("rubble_sorter", Vector2i(3,2), c + Vector2i(-8,-1), Vector2i(0,-1), 3)` and two scrap_collectors on the east trunk place cleanly with zero refusals; I measured that variant and it ran 52 crafts against the baseline's 40.

NOT MEASURED BY ME, AND MUST NOT BE READ OFF ANYTHING I RAN: perf. Four to five other Godot processes were on the box for most of this session. tests --part=citizens is 47 passed / 1 FAILED and the failure is test_a_thousand_citizens_fit_in_the_tick_budget at 5968 ms — a perf test on a loaded box. (The death-spiral test the previous F3 left red is now GREEN; [P05] fixed it.)

tools/check.sh was NOT run end to end (40+ min on a shared four-core box). I ran its parts: parse check, lint_sim, determinism.sh on both scenarios, a 24000-tick harness run with exit 0 and errors [], and the suites listed above including the standalone .tscn ones the --part flag silently skips.

tests/tutorial/run_tutorial.tscn with --force-ui takes well over two minutes and I could not get a second run of it inside a bounded command; the numbers I report for it are from one completed background run at HEAD. `--ui-tour` was reported hung by the previous F3 and I did not retry it — instead I photographed boot's real opening with tmp/f3/shot.tscn, which is 25 lines and works, and left it in tmp/f3 for whoever needs the first screen next.
